newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian business confidence rises - survey.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian business confidence rises - survey.

text.p: Australian business expectations rose in the September quarter after the 1996/97 budget and the July 31 interest rate cut, a survey found.

However, confidence remained below the levels reached after the March 2 election and manufacturing activity continued to decline, the Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ACCI) and Westpac Banking Corp survey released on Tuesday showed.

"Given that the budget was aimed at restoring business confidence...the results of the survey, in showing that manufacturing activity continued to ease, will be disappointing for the government," Westpac general manager economics Bill Evans said in a statement.
Evans said it was not surprising that confidence did not strengthen further as the budget, announced on August 20, was aimed at the medium-term.

"I don't think it was surprising that there wasn't a bigger jump in confidence because we have to accept that this budget is a medium term budget," Evans told reporters. "It's a budget with a two or three year outlook, rather than for the six months.

"Certainly, Westpac and a number of other economic commentators accept that in the very short term, the impact of the budget will probably be for a bit of a slow-down given the size of the cuts," Evans said.

"We're thinking more in terms of the eight to 10 percent range, but we are looking to see further growth in business investment particularly in the mining sector and the communications sector," he said.
The proportion of manufacturers expecting a decline in profits fell to 19 percent in the September quarter from 21 percent in the June quarter.
